text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Namibia's leadership and people want to strengthen ties with Vietnam, particularly in agriculture and trade, Namibian Foreign Minister Theo-Ben Gurirab told his Vietnamese counterpart Nguyen Manh Cam at a reception here on Saturday.
-- Water levels are rising early in the Mekong Delta this year. Last year about 100 people, mostly children, drowned and property and crops were destroyed.

-- A border pact to help create long-term peace, friendship and stability on land and in the Gulf of Tonkin will be signed between Vietnam and China soon, Vietnam's Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam said after returning from China last week.

-- Rice exporters must try their best to raise export rice prices to make them equal to worldwide prices, and increase the proportion of high-quality rice in the country's rice for export, Deputy Minister of Agricultural and Rural Development Nguyen Gioi said.

-- Vietnam held a big festival with more than 40 million voters on Sunday to vote for the tenth National Assembly. Nearly 99 percent of Hanoians and 99.61 percent of Ho Chi Minh City voters went to the polls.
-- Buddhist Monk, Thich Thien Hao, a former standing member of Vietnam's National Assembly and chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City Buddhist Association died on Sunday. He was 86.
-- Ho Chi Minh City has invested 547 billion dong ($46.8 million) in resettling people living in slums along the Nhieu Loc-Thi Nghe canal to 3,259 new houses.
